reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify that the refunds table matches what Alpha reported. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly: same three order IDs and amounts. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly. The orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
acme's net balance came back as 31766 cents, which I'll record once all balances are in. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Refunds match Alpha's report and I have acme and birch balances. Next I need cobalt's net balance.

I checked the net balances by hand against the orders and refunds, and all three match: acme 45425-13659=31766, birch 55259-19464=35795, cobalt 20917-9501=11416. The refunds also match Alpha's report, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 35795 cents, which I already verified against orders and refunds.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's balance of 11416 matches my hand check (orders 8761 + 12156 = 20917, minus refund 9501). Recording the last payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each returned ok. The refunds matched Alpha's report, and each amount matches the hand check against orders and refunds. The batch is complete.
